title: Adopt-A-Block through kids' eyes:
title_short: Adopt-A-Block · Life on Film · kids' eyes
headline: Two kids say they are happy and say what they love to do. Then a neighbor and two volunteers show what the day feels like.
story: The day is a Saturday on one city block. Children are part of it: Eliana passes out milk, Evan sits on the wall and says yes, he is happy. The kids open the film and the grown-ups finish it. The line, the neighbor at the car window, the volunteers. Series: Outrageous Generosity.

Loops: L1 “Why is she so happy?” opens 0:00 and closes at 0:23 on her message. L2 “How long was the line?” opens at 0:10 and closes at 0:17. Stakes: will the day, seen through a child's smile, show Dallas what a free Saturday feels like? The film stays on the day and on joy.
do: Open on Eliana's face with the hook text already on screen.
Keep the question in the cut every time a child answers.
Use the line, the hands and the banner as short cutaways. Pick the exact moment on scrub.
Name supers: first names only, small, lower left, 2 seconds.
Last line comes from a volunteer, Ethan.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
No trash, empty boxes or clutter in any shot. The client said so on the 1 Oct call.
No readable license plates in tight shots.
Nothing about anyone's circumstances. Do not use the food insecurity lines in Interview21.
Do not cut any child without a signed guardian release. See the open decisions.

Dream Center Dallas package in the Drive folder deliverables / graphics-packages. It has no logo files yet. Use the lower third bar, title plate and topic tag.

The transcript gives Eliana's file the label “Sara's Son”. She is a girl and says her name is Eliana. The lines of the interviewer and the child sit together in the transcript. Evan's own answers are missing from it, so only “Evan are you happy yes” is used.
tech: iPhone video, vertical 2160×3840 (stored 3840×2160 with a 90 degree rotation), 30 fps on the clips checked. Shot by Kalindi Cordero.
1080×1920 at 30 fps. Conform all clips to it.
All clips are already vertical. Keep each person in the middle third. Reframing from the 4K source is safe up to about 200 percent.

The clips checked have two audio tracks (2 channels and 4 channels). On Interview30 the first track carries the voice, mean about -20 dB. Check by ear which track is the DJI mic on each clip. Wind on the street clips: clean it. B-roll sound stays low under the voice.
Daylight, hard sun. Lift the shadows on faces a little. Keep skin warm.
-14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP peak. Music under the voice at all times.
Burned in on every spoken line. White bold sans (Montserrat until the client font arrives), low in the frame, phrase by phrase.
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920, 9:16. Upload to Frame.io, then Ready for Review.
checklist: Frame 1 is Eliana's face, already talking, with the hook text. No logo, name or fade.
The hook text is on screen at 0:00 and does not animate on.
Every child answer keeps its question in the cut.
No child is in the cut unless the release is signed. See the open decisions.
No trash, empty boxes or clutter in any B-roll shot. No readable license plates in tight shots.
Name supers are first names only, from 0:05, and each is on screen 2 seconds.
The food insecurity lines are not in the video.
The last line is Ethan's, a volunteer.
The end card has the Dream Center Dallas name or logo and the two lines.

decisions.b: The child's own camera card is not in the folder. Pass-DisposableFilm-Intro.MOV is an interview with Evan holding a microphone. It is not footage he shot. This cut uses Eliana (7) and Evan as the kid's-eye voice. Nick or Atdhe: say if the card exists or if another child is the one.
Eliana, Evan and any child in B-roll need a parent signature before the video goes out. Nick: is it signed? If not, tell Ardit and the cut changes to adults only.

decisions.t: Kids' answers are thin in the transcript
decisions.b: The transcript misses most of Evan's answers and Eliana's answer to “Why are you happy?”. Someone should listen to Pass 00:13 to 00:21 and Interview30 00:08 to 00:13. There may be a stronger line.
No visual reference on the Production Planning row. Nick owns it.
The client logo and font are not in Drive yet. Type the name on the end card.

client_note: Why this matters: Kacie asked for more personal and community shots and for something that moves people. This is the first cut from the day that opens on a child.
